headline: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: The committee began making decisions on the proposed fiscal year 27 county budget.
meeting.recap: The committee began making decisions on the proposed fiscal year 27 county budget.[[0:03:10]] The finance director reported $660,365,625 in property tax revenue, $156,548 more than the mayor's budget projected.[[0:08:39]] Properties in two wildfire-affected areas are back on the tax rolls, adding $7.4 million this year.[[0:20:22]] A testifier brought a proposal about a one-acre property on Kalani Road in Kīhei.[[0:23:51]] The committee chair proposed removing $3,441,584 in funding for new positions while keeping the positions.[[2:18:19]] Members voted 6 to 3 to bring department requests before the committee for a vote.[[4:32:39]]
decided: The committee approved a council member's farm-to-family program proposal.
The committee added a condition that grantees follow the food and nutrition security plan.
Members voted to bring department requests that were not member priorities before the committee for a vote.
The committee deleted $10,000 for Maui Search and Rescue.
meeting.next: Staff will track cuts, and members who vote for a cut that passes will share it equally for their priorities. Tomorrow's departments are environmental management, finance, fire, housing, human concerns, and liquor.

issues.oneLine: Long-term rental parcels grew to 4,350 from 3,223 last year.
issues.why: A testifier said women leaving shelter succeed depending on whether they can get stable housing.
issues.brief: The finance director said the long-term rental program reached its goal of about 5,000 applicants.[[#1]] A testifier brought a proposal about a one-acre property on Kalani Road in Kīhei.[[#2]] A testifier asked the county to help secure scattered housing sites for women leaving shelter.[[#3]]

issues.oneLine: An ordinance extends property tax relief for properties hit by the August 2023 wildfires.
issues.why: A council member said the tax data's 142 rebuilt dwellings do not show all the families who have returned home.
issues.brief: Properties in two wildfire-affected areas are back on the tax rolls, adding $7.4 million this year.[[#1]] The tax data lists 2,145 dwellings destroyed and 142 rebuilt.[[#2]] The finance director said full rebuilding counts would probably come from the Office of Recovery.[[#3]]
